pattern.crimePattern: a cardiologist billing insurers for stents never fitted kills the fraud investigator auditing his originals, and frames the grieving son who has threatened him online
pattern.notes: Fictional clinic, insurer and plaza. FORGERY (the procedure reports) and PLANTED (the son's key fob from the lost-and-found box) in one case. Spine background: a twelve-year-old photo of a launch "on the 4th floor" of the fictional Lands House, captioned with six officials (t_kivuli). Nothing in the case says which, if any, matters.

facts.text: Grace Mumbua, an insurance fraud investigator, was found dead in the records room of the Mwamburi Heart Centre on Wednesday morning.
One heavy blow to Grace's head. Files pulled out on the table.
The clinic's drugs cupboard is locked and untouched.
Under the body: a car key fob on a ring tagged "E. Karanja".
A steel drip stand in the corridor, its heavy round base wiped.
The receptionist: "It's that man Elvis. He's been threatening Daktari for months. He was outside with a placard yesterday."
Elvis's posts for eight months: "Mwamburi killed my father. He will pay."
Lost-and-found book: a car key fob tagged E. Karanja, found at reception two weeks ago, "in box". This morning the box has no fob.
Joan: unclaimed items stay in the box until collected; the box key is on the clinic's master ring.
Lobby camera: Elvis outside with a placard 18:00–18:50; he never comes in, and walks off towards the matatu stage.
Records ①: Dr. Mwamburi's card on the clinic floor at 20:31, out through the car park at 21:15. Grace signed in at 19:30. No other clinic card after 19:00.
Grace's sheet: 61 billed stents on dates the cath lab was closed for maintenance. "Originals Tuesday eve. If they match, refer to DCI."
The servicing company's record: the cath lab was closed for servicing on all 61 dates.
The files Grace pulled: procedure reports for stents on those very dates, signed by Dr. Mwamburi.
Benson's cath-lab log enters a stent procedure on each of the 61 dates.
Mama Eunice: Daktari's light was on at half past eight; at about quarter to nine a bang like a stand falling in the records room; Daktari came out and said, "Leave this floor tonight, Mama."
Mama Eunice went downstairs at 20:50 and stayed in the lobby (lobby camera).
Records ②: Imara paid the clinic KSh 38 million for the 61 stents.
In Dr. Mwamburi's office: a white coat in a dry-cleaning bag, blood on one cuff.
In his office: a folder of blank procedure-report forms, pre-signed with his stamped signature.
On his desk: the clinic's master ring, with the lost-and-found box key.
A twelve-year-old photo: "Launch of the Lands House Staff Medical Scheme, 4th Floor". Mwamburi among six officials, among them Raphael Oduya, Margaret Kabiru and Stanley Rotich.
The stage tout and his sister: Elvis took a matatu at 19:05 and was at his sister's in South B from 19:40 to midnight.
Benson was at the stadium for the evening match with three friends; his access card was unused after 17:00.
Joan was at choir practice 19:00–21:30.
Fingerprints taken from Dr. Mwamburi in detention.
Post-mortem: one blow from a heavy round metal base.
Post-mortem: death on Tuesday between 20:30 and 21:15.
Lab: the fob carries the reception box's lint (cardboard fibres, receipt-paper scraps) and none of the records room's dust.
Lab: Elvis's old, smudged prints on the fob, and a fresh partial of Dr. Mwamburi's on the ring.
Lab: the blood on the coat cuff is Grace's.
Questioned Documents Lab: the reports were printed from the same template as the pre-signed blanks, typed over a stamped facsimile signature.
Missing: the fob is no longer in the lost-and-found box.

reconstruction.text: For four years the clinic bills insurers for heart stents never fitted: a diagnostic test, then a procedure report typed on a pre-signed blank. Benson keeps the cath-lab log to match.
Grace notices that 61 billed stents fall on days the servicing company had the cath lab closed. She arranges to see the originals on Tuesday evening. "We have nothing to hide," says Dr. Mwamburi.

At 20:31 his card comes back on the floor. At about quarter to nine he finds her with the reports pulled out and strikes her with the steel base of a drip stand. He tells Mama Eunice to leave the floor.
He takes Elvis's lost key fob from the reception box (the key is on his ring) and drops it under her. He leaves through the car park at 21:15. In the morning the staff name the man with the placard.

afterVerdict.beat: Elvis is cleared. Imara refers all 61 claims to the DCI; the clinic's licence is suspended. Benson is charged with fraud.
The boardroom photograph is auto-filed to the Pattern File. Amani's notebook: "Fourth floor, Lands House. Six faces. Photographed."

clockPlan.note: Three stamps, the maximum: the plaza access log (which also reopens Dr. Mwamburi), Imara's claim payments, and a warrant on his office. The fob's dust trace (12 h) goes first thing; the document exam (10 h) and cuff blood (12 h) go after the search; detain him, and the prints (6 h) and blood are back inside 24 h.
